memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Marcus selected a Monday evening Midway-to-Nashville nonstop for comparison and retained two Tuesday Midway returns: an earlier flight feasible after a 4:00 p.m. supplier-meeting finish and a later flight with adequate margin if the meeting runs until 5:30 p.m. No booking was made.

messages.content: I need Nashville next week for a Tuesday morning operating review. I can leave Chicago after work Monday, and there is a supplier meeting Tuesday that might end at 4:00 or could drag to 5:30. Show me practical round trips, but do not book anything.
What dates are Monday and Tuesday, and where will you be leaving from after work? That will determine whether O'Hare or Midway is actually faster door to door.
Monday March 16 and Tuesday March 17. I'll be at our West Loop office near Randolph and Halsted. The review is at 9:00 Tuesday near Broadway and West End.

From that office, allow roughly 35-55 minutes to Midway or 45-75 minutes to O'Hare in Monday traffic, plus airport time. Nashville airport is usually 15-25 minutes from the restaurant area without a major traffic delay. I would avoid departures before about 6:30 p.m. What time can you leave the office?
Around 4:45. Nonstop only. I do not need the absolute cheapest fare if the schedule is bad.

The cleanest outbound is Southwest from Midway at 7:05 p.m., arriving Nashville at 8:35 p.m. Central. A comparable O'Hare choice is American at 7:40 p.m., arriving at 9:13 p.m. The Midway itinerary gives you more margin from the office and gets you to the hotel about 40 minutes earlier. Current round-trip pricing depends on which return you pair with it, but the useful combinations are running about $278-$346 in standard economy fares.
Use the Midway outbound. What are the Tuesday returns if I want one aggressive option and one that covers a late meeting?

For an on-time 4:00 p.m. finish, Southwest has a 6:20 p.m. nonstop from Nashville to Midway, arriving at 8:00 p.m. You would need to leave the meeting by about 4:35 p.m. to allow 25 minutes for the drive and reach the terminal around 5:00. That pairing is about $294 round trip. It works, but it is not a good choice if the meeting reaches 5:30.
And the protected option? I do not want a connection just to get home that night.

The later practical nonstop is Southwest at 8:45 p.m., arriving Midway at 10:25 p.m. A 5:30 finish would let you leave around 5:45, reach BNA near 6:10, and still have more than two hours before departure. Paired with the same Monday flight, it is about $326 round trip.
Is there anything from O'Hare that is meaningfully better on the return?

American has a 7:35 p.m. nonstop to O'Hare, arriving about 9:25 p.m. It falls between the two Midway choices, but a 5:30 meeting finish would leave only about 80 minutes at the airport if traffic is normal. It also returns you to O'Hare rather than where you departed, so it is only attractive if someone is dropping you at Midway Monday or you will not leave a car there.

No car. Still, the 7:35 sounds too tight if they run late. Keep this simple: carry forward the Monday Midway flight and both Midway returns. Also tell me when I would realistically reach the restaurant area Monday night.

Carrying forward these three candidates: Monday March 16, Southwest MDW-BNA at 7:05 p.m., arriving 8:35 p.m.; Tuesday March 17, Southwest BNA-MDW at 6:20 p.m., arriving 8:00 p.m.; and the protected return at 8:45 p.m., arriving 10:25 p.m. After landing Monday, allow about 20-30 minutes to exit and reach a rideshare, then 15-25 minutes to the Broadway/West End area. A realistic hotel arrival is 9:15-9:30 p.m. Nothing has been booked.
